# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 89 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 50 | Coptic

---

## Saying 89

Jesus said: "Why do you wash the outside of the cup? Do you not understand that he who made the inside is also he who made the outside?"

---

**Council Notes:**

- Thomas's cup-washing saying (cf. Matt 23:25-26; Luke 11:39-40) strips the Synoptic moral condemnation and focuses on a creator-unity argument: the same maker made both inside and outside.
- This transforms the saying from an anti-Pharisee polemic into a cosmological statement: you cannot treat the inside and outside as belonging to different creators.
- This may be a subtle anti-Gnostic or anti-Marcionite point: the material outside is not made by a lesser demiurge; the same creator made both.
- "He who made" preserved (EMET) — the personal maker language is important; PNEUMA's "whoever" is too neutral.
